data.name: Aloisio
data.gender_notes: Aloisio is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Aloisio is derived from the Latin word 'Aloysius', which means 'not Olaf, but another kind of all wolf'. The name became popular during the Middle Ages due to the widespread veneration of St. Aloysius Gonzaga, who is known for his deep spirituality, piety, and self-sacrifice. Aloisio can be translated as 'noble and army warrior'.
data.etymology: Aloisio belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Noble and army warrior.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aloisio total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_hebrew.name: עלואיש
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עלואיש הוא שם ילד נוצרי, נובע מהשם הנוצרי הגרמני Aloisio. שם זה התגלה בימי הביניים. עלואיש נחשב לשם ילד נבון וחכם, ונפוץ בעיקר בקהילות נוצריות. עלואיש הוא גם שם נפוץ בקרב יהודים ונוצרים, ומיוחס לאישים חשובים באותם זמנים.

in_greek.name: Αλοίσιο
in_greek.long_meaning: Αλοίσιο είναι χριστιανικό όνομα, προέρχεται από το γερμανικό όνομα Aloisio. Το όνομα αυτό εμφανίστηκε στη μεσαιωνική εποχή. Αλοίσιο θεωρείται όνομα για παιδιά σοφά και έξυπνα, και είναι ιδιαίτερα δημοφιλές στις χριστιανικές κοινότητες. Αλοίσιο είναι επίσης ένα phổ biến όνομα μεταξύ Εβραίων και Χριστιανών, και συνδέεται με σημαντικούς ανθρώπους της εποχής.

in_latin.name: Aloisio
in_latin.long_meaning: Aloisio est nomen christianum, originem habet ab nomine germanico Aloisio. Nomen hoc apparuit in tempore mediaevi. Aloisio reputatur nomen puerorum sapientibus et prudentibus, et est frequentius in usu in communitatibus christianis. Aloisio est etiam nomen commune inter Judaeos et Christianos, et attribuitur hominibus magnis in eadem aetate.

data.cultural_impact: The name Aloisio has historical significance due to its association with St. Aloysius Gonzaga, who was a Jesuit priest and a member of the influential Gonzaga family. St. Aloysius is venerated as the patron saint of students, those with contagious diseases, the young dying, victims of infectious diseases, and athletes. The name gained popularity in Christian communities during the Middle Ages, and it is still used in various parts of the world today. It is a name deeply rooted in Catholic tradition and values.

This patron saint of students and those with contagious diseases embodies the Christian virtues of piety, self-sacrifice, and spiritual awareness. Aloisio can be a reminder to live our lives with deep spiritual attention, dedicating ourselves to the service of others and embracing the challenges we face with a courageous and faith-filled heart.
